generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the research you are already doing or about to begin. Every ethics application you complete, every participant whose data you protect, and every decision you can defend to an examiner draws on the same habits. People who treat ethics, data and rigour as things they own, rather than boxes to tick, are the ones whose work can be trusted. Treat what follows as being about your own project and dissertation, not about research in the abstract.

The same habits run through professional practice. Wherever work gathers data from people, is judged against a standard, and must be accounted for, those who are trusted are the ones whose integrity can be shown rather than merely asserted. The discipline you build here is one you keep long after you graduate.
